newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises power, fuel and telephone prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises power, fuel and telephone prices.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government on Thursday raised power, fuel and telephone prices to keep up with the lev's fall against the dollar.
A government spokeswoman said the cabinet raised the prices of electricity, coal and heating by 257 percent, effective from March 1.
Diesel, petrol and other fuel prices will rise by 8.15 percent from Friday and telephone charges will rise by 525 percent from March 1.
Interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said the price rises would affect the prices of other goods including foodstuffs.
"The government hopes that by mid-March financial stabilisation will be achieved and measures will be taken against speculative price hikes in an attempt to ease the shock," Sofianski told reporters.
The cabinet has unblocked heating prices after the previous government of the Socialists froze them last October due to the hardship they cause to ordinary people.
Since July, energy prices have been revised each month, mainly according to the inflation rate and the lev/dollar exchange rate.
Energy officials said international lending institutions had recommended a target electricity rate of 3.5 cents per kilowatt hour, while it was currently less than 1.5 cents.

Bulgaria suffers severe fuel shortages and the interim government raised fuel prices by up to 178 percent on February 17 in a bid to free suppliers' volumes kept in storage. It also banned fuel exports until April 30.
Telephone rates were last raised on January 1 but remain among the lowest in Europe.
